title: Why Broken QR Codes Still Work
description:
Why broken QR codes still work: error correction, the 1:1:3:1:1 finder ratio, and how many QR codes can exist.

A 90-second music-only film. No voice, no one on camera: the type and the pictures carry it. A QR code with a piece missing can still be read, because the code carries extra data that rebuilds what was lost. The film follows that from 1994 to the count of every digit-only code that fits in the biggest size, which is at least 10^7,089 (version 40-L, digits only, a floor: letters, bytes, other sizes and other levels would add more).

0:00 Partly missing, it still reads
0:10 Where it started
0:22 The rarest ratio
0:35 How the code grew
0:52 From 12 digits to 10^7,089 codes
1:14 How a damaged code is rebuilt

The QR codes drawn in the film are illustrations. Larger sizes are plausible patterns, not readable codes.

The count: a version 40, level L code holds up to 7,089 digits. Each digit has 10 choices, so there are 10 x 10 x ... (7,089 times) = 10^7,089 different digit-only messages. "QR Code" is a registered trademark of DENSO WAVE.
